title: Minimum Effective Dose
hook: I was writing 3,000-word newsletters. The 600-word ones got more replies.
statement: Find the least effort that still gets the result. Everything past that point is waste.
explainer: More effort feels safer, but it often adds nothing. Overbuilding burns time and energy you could put somewhere that actually moves the needle.
sop: Pick one recurring effort you suspect is overbuilt.
Rate its current Result and Effort from 1 to 10.
Cut the effort roughly in half for 2 weeks, same goal.
Re-rate the Result. Did it actually drop?
If it held, keep the lighter version for good.
equation_example: Result 8, Effort 4. 8 ÷ 4 = 2.0. You're getting twice the result per unit of effort. Higher means you've found the right dose. Below 1 means you're pouring in more than you get back.
question: Name one thing you're overbuilding that would work just as well at half the effort.
closing_statement: Effort past what works is just waste.
caption:
Principle Nº 156: Minimum Effective Dose

I was writing 3,000-word newsletters. The 600-word ones got more replies.

Find the least effort that still gets the result. Everything past that point is waste.

Your turn: Name one thing you're overbuilding that would work just as well at half the effort.
